# LokalBot **Your personal context engine.** Private meeting notes, workday recall, dictation, and autocomplete—with AI that runs on your computer.
Your AI agents can search it too, from Claude Code, Codex, or any MCP client.
Free and open source. No account. Nothing joins your calls. [![Download LokalBot for macOS](https://img.shields.io/badge/%E2%80%82Download%20for%20macOS%E2%80%82-Apple%20Silicon-0969da?style=for-the-badge&logo=apple&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot/releases/latest) [![Download LokalBot for Windows (alpha)](https://img.shields.io/badge/%E2%80%82Download%20for%20Windows%E2%80%82-alpha-0969da?style=for-the-badge&logo=data%3Aimage%2Fsvg%2Bxml%3Bbase64%2CPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0naHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmcnIHZpZXdCb3g9JzAgMCAxNiAxNic%2BPHBhdGggZmlsbD0nd2hpdGUnIGQ9J00wIDBoNy41djcuNUgwek04LjUgMEgxNnY3LjVIOC41ek0wIDguNWg3LjVWMTZIMHpNOC41IDguNUgxNlYxNkg4LjV6Jy8%2BPC9zdmc%2B)](https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot/releases/latest) [![Download LokalBot for Linux (alpha)](https://img.shields.io/badge/%E2%80%82Download%20for%20Linux%E2%80%82-alpha-0969da?style=for-the-badge&logo=linux&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot/releases/latest) Apple Silicon (M1 or later) with macOS 15+ · Windows 10/11 x64 (alpha) · Linux x86_64 (alpha) · on Mac, also brew install --cask stevyhacker/tap/lokalbot [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/stevyhacker/lokalbot?color=1f6feb&label=release)](https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot/releases/latest) [![License: GPLv3](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPLv3-2ea043)](LICENSE) [![MCP: read-only server](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-read--only%20server-8250df)](#for-developers--agents) ⭐ If LokalBot is useful to you, star the repo. It's built by one developer, and stars are how other people find it. **English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) [Features](#features) · [Windows & Linux](#windows-and-linux) · [Compare](#how-it-compares) · [Privacy](#privacy) · [Get started](#get-started) · [Models](#local-ai-your-choice) · [Agents & CLI](#for-developers--agents) · [Website](https://www.lokalbot.com/) The real app, recorded with fictional demo data.

45 seconds: why LokalBot keeps what you heard and saw, which local models do the work, then the real app in use. Fictional demo data.
## Features ### Remember what was agreed Record microphone and meeting-app audio without a bot joining. Get local transcripts, recaps, decisions, and action items, with citations back to the discussion.
### Find something you saw One search across your meeting transcripts and, if you turn it on, what you saw on screen. Search by keyword or by meaning, then open the matching passage or screen moment instead of hunting through apps. The same window (**⌃⇧ Space**, or **Ctrl+Shift+Space** on Windows and Linux, once you turn on the shortcut in **Settings → General**) also runs app commands such as **Record now** or **Start dictation** from whatever app you're in.
### Finish the sentence As you type in other apps, gray text suggests how your sentence ends. Press **Tab** to take the next word, **\`** to take the rest on Mac, or keep typing.
Live suggestions in TextEdit, in real time. The ship date and condition come from the meeting with John. Fictional demo meeting.
- **Knows what you're answering.** It reads the message or page above the field, so a reply fits the thread. - **Remembers your meetings, if you let it.** Turn on meeting and work memory, and it can bring in what was decided, like the ship date above. - **Writes in your language.** On Mac, the same small model keeps up in German, French, Italian, Spanish, and more. - **Stays on your computer.** A small model runs inside the app: Gemma 4 E2B on Mac, LFM2.5 1.2B on Windows and Linux. What you type and the context it reads never leave your computer. Turn it on in **Settings → Writing**, where you can try it on a sample conversation first and later see how much it wrote for you. ### Pick up where you left off Today brings your day digest and open meeting actions together. Timeline groups captured activity into work sessions, with the underlying context available to inspect. Correct actions, mark them done, and trace each one to its source.
Today: your digest and open actions Timeline: work sessions and their context
### Talk instead of typing Turn on Dictation in **Settings → Dictation**, then hold **⌥ Space** (**Alt+Space** on Windows and Linux, or a shortcut you choose there), speak, and release to insert text at your cursor in any app. Transcription runs on your computer. On Wayland, bind `lokalbot dictate` to a shortcut in your desktop's settings. ### Rewrite what you selected Turn on selection actions in **Settings → General**, select text in any app, and press **⌃⇧ W**. Fix the grammar, make it shorter, translate it, summarize it, or type your own instruction, then replace the selection or copy the result. **Draft a reply with my memory** also searches your meetings, so the reply can use what was actually agreed, and lists the meetings it used. It runs on your Think model, which stays on your Mac unless you chose and approved a server. Selection actions are on Mac only for now. ### And more | Ask, then check the source | Follow through | Bring your own agent | | --- | --- | --- | | Ask about your meeting library and follow the answer's citations back to the transcript or audio. Generated notes are a starting point, not a substitute for the discussion. | Prepare local follow-up drafts. On Mac, also keep a note for every meeting in your Obsidian or Logseq folder, and get daily briefs and weekly work logs. You review and send them yourself. | Give Claude Code or any MCP client read-only access to your meeting library through the bundled `lokalbot-cli`. It stays off until you enable it. | Screenshots are unedited captures of the Mac app with fictional demo data. They show the interface, not a live inference benchmark. The Autocomplete clip is a cropped, real-time recording of live suggestions. Click an image for full resolution; see the capture notes for provenance. ### Also on Windows and Linux (alpha) A native Windows and Linux app, written in Rust, has the same pages and reads the same library, so a library moves between computers. Meetings, transcription, Ask, search, day memory, screen context, dictation, autocomplete, calendar, Agent Mode, and the CLI and MCP server all work. It's an alpha: the Windows build isn't code-signed yet, some features depend on your Linux desktop (Wayland support is partial), and a few Mac features haven't been ported. See [what works where](LinuxWindows/README.md#what-works-where) and [screenshots](LinuxWindows/docs/screenshots). ## How it compares | Coming from… | What's different with LokalBot | | --- | --- | | [Granola](https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-granola) | The same bot-free capture, but transcription and summaries run on your computer by default. No account and no subscription. | | [Apple Notes](https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-apple-notes) | Notes records your microphone, so with headphones on it misses the other side of a Zoom or Teams call. LokalBot records both sides and keeps every meeting searchable, with notes that cite the discussion. | | [Otter](https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-otter) · [Fireflies](https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-fireflies) | Nothing joins your call, audio stays on your computer, and there are no minute caps. | | [Hyprnote (anarlog)](https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-hyprnote) | Local AI ships built in, with no separate model runner or API keys to set up. Dictation, a day timeline, and autocomplete come in the same app. | | [Meetily](https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-meetily) | Both are open source and run locally. Speaker separation, meeting detection, and MCP access are free here rather than Pro features, and dictation, a day timeline, and autocomplete come in the same app. | | [Screenpipe](https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-screenpipe) | Starts with app and window activity. Screen text and screenshots are opt-in and deleted after 14 days by default. GPLv3 rather than source-available. | | [Rewind](https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-rewind) | Rewind's Mac app is discontinued. LokalBot's timeline is open source and actively developed. | | [MacWhisper](https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-macwhisper) · [Superwhisper](https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-superwhisper) | Dictation comes alongside meeting notes, recall, and autocomplete, for free. For transcribing files you already have, MacWhisper is the better tool. | | [Wispr Flow](https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-wispr-flow) | Dictation and bot-free meeting notes run on your computer, with no account, word cap, or connection required. Wispr Flow transcribes both in its cloud. | Competitor details were last verified on September 24, 2026, and October 1, 2026 for Apple Notes, Meetily, and Wispr Flow; each link has the full comparison and sources. Trademarks belong to their owners. ## Privacy **Your work is personal. Keeping it local should be the starting point.** Recording and built-in AI processing happen on your computer. LokalBot has no account system, analytics service, or telemetry backend. Your library lives in local files and SQLite under your user account. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph mac [Your computer] direction LR audio["Mic + meeting-app audio"] --> asr["On-device
transcription"] asr --> llm["Local summaries
built-in llama.cpp"] screen["Opt-in screen text"] --> db[("Local library
full-text + vector search")] asr --> db llm --> db db --> use["Search · Ask · Today · Timeline"] db -.->|read-only, off by default| cli["lokalbot-cli · MCP"] end ``` - **You choose what to retain.** Activity-only tracking is the default. Visible screen text and encrypted screenshots are opt-in. Pause capture or exclude apps and domains at any time. Detection has limits; exclude anything you never want retained. - **You control retention.** Captured screen text and screenshots expire after 14 days by default. Adjust the window or explicitly save a moment to keep it until you unsave or delete it. - **Network access has boundaries.** Models, updates, and optional agent runtimes need downloads. Automatic update checks can be disabled. A remote model server receives context only after you approve its origin; optional Agent Mode and external CLI/MCP clients have separate permissions and data handling. To check the local processing path, download the models, select the built-in backend, disable automatic update checks, and observe network traffic while recording, transcribing, and summarizing. Approved agent commands and external clients are separate paths. [Read the full privacy policy](PRIVACY.md) · [Report a security issue privately](SECURITY.md) ## Get started LokalBot runs on Apple Silicon Macs with macOS 15 or later. Windows and Linux are in alpha. You'll also need space for your selected models: **Settings → Models** shows download sizes and readiness, and storage and memory needs depend on the models you choose. | | macOS | Windows (alpha) | Linux (alpha) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Runs on | Apple Silicon (M1 or later), macOS 15+ | Windows 10 or 11, x64 | x86_64 with glibc 2.39 or later (Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Fedora 40 or newer), PulseAudio or PipeWire, and a Vulkan or OpenGL driver | | Install | [`LokalBot--macos-arm64.dmg`](https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot/releases/latest): drag LokalBot to Applications. Or `brew install --cask stevyhacker/tap/lokalbot`. | [`LokalBot--windows-x86_64-setup.exe`](https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot/releases/latest): run it to install LokalBot for your user, with a Start menu shortcut and no administrator rights. It isn't code-signed yet, so SmartScreen asks first: **More info → Run anyway**. The same release has a portable zip. | [`LokalBot--linux-x86_64.tar.gz`](https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot/releases/latest): extract it and run `./install.sh`, which adds LokalBot to your applications menu. Or install the `.deb` (Debian, Ubuntu), `.rpm` (Fedora, openSUSE) or Arch package from the same release. The `.deb`, and the `.rpm` on Fedora, add the LokalBot repository, so `sudo apt upgrade` or `sudo dnf upgrade` brings later versions; with the Arch package, LokalBot tells you about updates instead of installing them. | | Your library | `~/Library/Application Support/me.dotenv.LokalBot` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\LokalBot` | `~/.local/share/LokalBot` | A library recorded on one platform opens on the others. Not every Mac feature is on Windows and Linux yet; see [what works where](LinuxWindows/README.md#what-works-where). 1. **Install the app** for your platform and open it. 2. **Choose what to capture.** Review recording settings: automatic detection, ask-first, or manual recording. Day tracking starts with activity only; saving screen text or screenshots is a separate opt-in. Grant only the permissions for the features you enable. 3. **Let the models download.** Built-in transcription, search, summaries, and writing can then work offline. No model server to set up and no API key to bring. **Try this first:** make a short test recording, let it transcribe, then search for a phrase you said and open the matching passage. Add screen memory or writing tools when you're ready. Let meeting participants know before recording and get their consent. [Release notes](https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot/releases) · [Setup help](SUPPORT.md) · [Homebrew options](Distribution/homebrew/README.md) · [Windows and Linux guide](LinuxWindows/README.md) ## FAQ
Does a bot join my meetings? No. LokalBot records your microphone and the meeting app's audio on your computer. On Windows and Linux it records everything the computer plays, not one app. Audio sources are separate from individual speaker identification. When system-audio capture is unavailable, the app warns that recording is microphone-only. Always record with participants' consent.
Does it record everything on my screen? No. New installs use activity-only tracking, which you can turn off. Saving visible text or screenshots requires a separate choice and the relevant macOS permissions (on Linux, your desktop's accessibility and screenshot support). Excluded apps and domains and secure fields are skipped; private browser windows are captured unless you exclude the browser or site. Detected credentials are redacted and associated pixels are dropped, but detection is not perfect. See [PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md).
Can I take my notes elsewhere? Yes. On Mac, turn on **Meeting note export** to keep a Markdown note for every meeting in a folder you choose, such as an Obsidian vault or a Logseq graph: the summary, action items, the people and projects involved, and the transcript. You can also export a single meeting, write a daily memory note, or let local routines save drafts. These are ordinary, unencrypted files; any service you sync them with has its own privacy settings. See [Meeting transcripts in Obsidian](https://www.lokalbot.com/meeting-transcripts-obsidian-markdown). Note export isn't on Windows and Linux yet.
Does it run on Windows or Linux? Yes, as an alpha. The Windows and Linux app is a native Rust app with the same pages, the same models for summaries and search, and the same library format, so a library moves between computers. Selection actions, meeting note export, Personal Context, spoken summaries, and coding-agent sessions in day memory are Mac only for now, and on Wayland some features depend on your desktop. See [what works where](LinuxWindows/README.md#what-works-where).
## Local AI, your choice Start with the built-in models, then change them in **Settings → Models**. LokalBot supports its bundled llama.cpp runtime, Ollama, OpenAI-compatible servers, and Apple Intelligence on supported Macs running macOS 26 or later. Think can also run on your own ChatGPT plan (Sign in with ChatGPT) or Claude plan (through your signed-in Claude Code), without an API key, and Agent Mode can run on the ChatGPT plan. Remote servers and plans require approval before receiving context. Different jobs use different models. These are the Mac defaults on a fresh install, about 9.6 GB of model files if you use every role. They are not a RAM requirement: | Role | Default model | Format | Approx. model files | | --- | --- | --- | ---: | | Transcription | Qwen3-ASR 1.7B | MLX 8-bit | 2.47 GB | | Summaries and chat | Qwen3.5 4B | `Q4_K_M` | 2.74 GB | | Autocomplete | Gemma 4 E2B Base | `Q6_K` | 3.85 GB | | Semantic search | EmbeddingGemma 2 | `Q8_0` | 0.31 GB | | Speaker diarization | Nemotron 3 (preview) via FluidAudio | Core ML | ~0.20 GB | Qwen3-ASR covers 52 languages and dialects. Transcription alternatives include Parakeet, Granite Speech, Whisper large-v3 turbo, SenseVoice for Chinese, Japanese, and Korean, and GigaAM for Russian; Pyannote Community-1 remains available for diarization. The Lightweight preset swaps in smaller models, including LFM2.5 1.2B Instruct (0.73 GB) for autocomplete. Model choices can vary by release; Settings shows the active selections and available presets. Speed and memory use depend on your computer, model, context length, and other workloads. On Windows and Linux, transcription uses Qwen3-ASR 0.6B through sherpa-onnx (Parakeet v3, SenseVoice, and Whisper turbo are optional), speakers are separated with pyannote segmentation and TitaNet, and autocomplete uses LFM2.5 1.2B by default. Summaries (Qwen3.5 4B) and search (EmbeddingGemma 2) use the same models as on Mac. The default download is about 4 GB, and llama.cpp runs on a Vulkan GPU or the CPU. [Project benchmarks](Benchmarks/README.md) · [Model catalog](LokalBot/Engines/ModelCatalog.swift) · [Search implementation](LokalBot/Services/EmbeddingIndex.swift) · [Model and runtime details](DEVELOPMENT.md#built-in-llm-runtime--llamacpp--model-catalog) ## For developers & agents The app bundles **`lokalbot-cli`**, a read-only interface to your meeting library and a stdio **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** server. Access is off by default. Enable meeting-library access in **Settings → Privacy & Data**, then install the CLI from **Settings → Advanced → Agent CLI**.
```bash lokalbot-cli search "database decision" lokalbot-cli get latest --include metadata,summary lokalbot-cli mcp ``` Without a PATH installation, use `/Applications/LokalBot.app/Contents/Helpers/lokalbot-cli` on Mac. On Windows and Linux, **Settings → Advanced → Agent CLI** installs it too; see [Coding agents](LinuxWindows/README.md#coding-agents) for where it goes and how to add it to your PATH. There the CLI has the read-only commands and every MCP tool; `ask`, `reply`, and the setup and configuration commands are Mac only. Connect Claude Code with one command, or install the [Claude Code plugin](Distribution/claude-plugin/README.md): ```bash # macOS claude mcp add lokalbot -- /Applications/LokalBot.app/Contents/Helpers/lokalbot-cli mcp # Windows and Linux, with lokalbot-cli on your PATH claude mcp add lokalbot -- lokalbot-cli mcp ``` Screen-memory MCP tools require separate permission scoped to today, the last seven days, or all retained history. They return text and metadata, not decrypted screenshots. External clients may send results to their own model providers. The app also has an optional **Agent Mode** for working with reviewed context. File and shell actions follow its approval settings; it is separate from the read-only CLI/MCP interface. [CLI examples](.agents/skills/lokalbot-cli/SKILL.md) · [Claude Code plugin](Distribution/claude-plugin/README.md) · [MCP architecture](DEVELOPMENT.md#agent-cli--mcp) ## Build from source For the Mac app, use an Apple Silicon Mac with full Xcode installed; the [build workflow](.github/workflows/build.yml) pins the CI toolchain. With Homebrew available: ```bash brew install xcodegen cmake git clone https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot.git cd lokalbot # XcodeGen needs these paths before the first build fetches the runtimes. mkdir -p Vendor/llama-cpp Vendor/sherpa-onnx xcodegen generate open LokalBot.xcodeproj ``` Select **LokalBot Dev**, set your signing team, and run. The Dev app has its own identity, macOS permission grants, library, model storage, and Keychain namespace, so it can live alongside the installed release without applying development retention settings to release data. The first build prepares pinned native runtimes; model downloads happen separately. For the Windows and Linux app, see [Build from source](LinuxWindows/README.md#build-from-source) in its README (Rust). [Build and test commands](DEVELOPMENT.md#build-workflows) · [Testing guide](DEVELOPMENT.md#testing) · [Screenshot guide](Docs/screenshot-kit.md)
Find your way around the code ```text LokalBot/ ├── Views/ # Native SwiftUI screens, settings, and onboarding ├── Services/ # Recording, search, storage, and workday memory ├── Engines/ # Transcription, model catalog, and local inference ├── Cotyping/ # System-wide autocomplete ├── Dictation/ # Voice typing └── Agent/ # Optional Agent Mode and approval flow CLI/ # Command-line interface and MCP entry points LinuxWindows/ # Windows and Linux app (Rust + GPUI) LokalBotTests/ # Unit tests Scripts/ # Build, verification, capture, and release tooling project.yml # XcodeGen source of truth ```
## Contributing Bug reports, documentation improvements, and code contributions are welcome. [Report an issue](https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot/issues/new/choose) with steps to reproduce, expected and actual behavior, the app version, your OS and its version (on Linux, also the distribution, desktop, and X11 or Wayland), your chip or CPU and GPU, RAM, and selected models. Keep private recordings and transcripts out of reports. For larger changes, [open an issue](https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot/issues) to discuss the approach first. Follow the [working agreements](AGENTS.md) and [development guide](DEVELOPMENT.md), keep pull requests focused, and record your checks in the [PR template](.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md). Include screenshots for UI changes; run UI tests on hosted CI or a remote runner. ## License & acknowledgements LokalBot is free software under [GPLv3](LICENSE). Code in the Autocomplete engine that was ported from [Cotabby](https://github.com/FuJacob/cotabby) stays under [AGPLv3](LICENSES/AGPL-3.0.txt). Other third-party components and models retain their own licenses; see [third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). Built with [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp), [MLX Swift](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-swift), [speech-swift](https://github.com/soniqo/speech-swift), [sherpa-onnx](https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx), [WhisperKit](https://github.com/argmaxinc/WhisperKit), [FluidAudio](https://github.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio), [Sparkle](https://github.com/sparkle-project/Sparkle), [XcodeGen](https://github.com/yonaskolb/XcodeGen), [GPUI](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/tree/main/crates/gpui), [GPUI Kit](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-kit), and [ONNX Runtime](https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime), with models including [Qwen3-ASR](https://huggingface.co/Qwen), [IBM Granite Speech](https://huggingface.co/ibm-granite), [Parakeet](https://huggingface.co/nvidia), and [LFM2.5](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI). The Autocomplete engine started from [Cotabby](https://cotabby.app)'s open-source code.

Today brings your day digest and open meeting actions together. Timeline groups captured activity into work sessions, with the underlying context available to inspect. Correct actions, mark them done, and trace each one to its source.

<table>

<tr>

<td width="50%"><a href="Assets/screenshots/today.png"><img src="Assets/screenshots/today.png" alt="Today showing the day digest and outstanding meeting actions" width="400" /></a></td>

<td width="50%"><a href="Assets/screenshots/timeline.png"><img src="Assets/screenshots/timeline.png" alt="Timeline showing work sessions, meetings, and access to captured context" width="400" /></a></td>

</tr>

<tr>

<td align="center"><sub><b>Today</b>: your digest and open actions</sub></td>

<td align="center"><sub><b>Timeline</b>: work sessions and their context</sub></td>

</tr>

</table>

Talk instead of typing

Turn on Dictation in Settings → Dictation, then hold ⌥ Space (Alt+Space on Windows and Linux, or a shortcut you choose there), speak, and release to insert text at your cursor in any app. Transcription runs on your computer. On Wayland, bind lokalbot dictate to a shortcut in your desktop's settings.

Rewrite what you selected

Turn on selection actions in Settings → General, select text in any app, and press ⌃⇧ W. Fix the grammar, make it shorter, translate it, summarize it, or type your own instruction, then replace the selection or copy the result. Draft a reply with my memory also searches your meetings, so the reply can use what was actually agreed, and lists the meetings it used. It runs on your Think model, which stays on your Mac unless you chose and approved a server. Selection actions are on Mac only for now.

And more

| Ask, then check the source | Follow through | Bring your own agent |

| --- | --- | --- |

| Ask about your meeting library and follow the answer's citations back to the transcript or audio. Generated notes are a starting point, not a substitute for the discussion. | Prepare local follow-up drafts. On Mac, also keep a note for every meeting in your Obsidian or Logseq folder, and get daily briefs and weekly work logs. You review and send them yourself. | Give Claude Code or any MCP client read-only access to your meeting library through the bundled lokalbot-cli. It stays off until you enable it. |

<sub>Screenshots are unedited captures of the Mac app with fictional demo data. They show the interface, not a live inference benchmark. The Autocomplete clip is a cropped, real-time recording of live suggestions. Click an image for full resolution; see the <a href="Assets/screenshots/README.md">capture notes</a> for provenance.</sub>

<a id="windows-and-linux"></a>

Also on Windows and Linux (alpha)

A native Windows and Linux app, written in Rust, has the same pages and reads the same library, so a library moves between computers. Meetings, transcription, Ask, search, day memory, screen context, dictation, autocomplete, calendar, Agent Mode, and the CLI and MCP server all work. It's an alpha: the Windows build isn't code-signed yet, some features depend on your Linux desktop (Wayland support is partial), and a few Mac features haven't been ported. See [what works where](LinuxWindows/README.md#what-works-where) and [screenshots](LinuxWindows/docs/screenshots).

How it compares

| Coming from… | What's different with LokalBot |

| --- | --- |

| Granola | The same bot-free capture, but transcription and summaries run on your computer by default. No account and no subscription. |

| Apple Notes | Notes records your microphone, so with headphones on it misses the other side of a Zoom or Teams call. LokalBot records both sides and keeps every meeting searchable, with notes that cite the discussion. |

| Otter · Fireflies | Nothing joins your call, audio stays on your computer, and there are no minute caps. |

| Hyprnote (anarlog) | Local AI ships built in, with no separate model runner or API keys to set up. Dictation, a day timeline, and autocomplete come in the same app. |

| Meetily | Both are open source and run locally. Speaker separation, meeting detection, and MCP access are free here rather than Pro features, and dictation, a day timeline, and autocomplete come in the same app. |

| Screenpipe | Starts with app and window activity. Screen text and screenshots are opt-in and deleted after 14 days by default. GPLv3 rather than source-available. |

| Rewind | Rewind's Mac app is discontinued. LokalBot's timeline is open source and actively developed. |

| MacWhisper · Superwhisper | Dictation comes alongside meeting notes, recall, and autocomplete, for free. For transcribing files you already have, MacWhisper is the better tool. |

| Wispr Flow | Dictation and bot-free meeting notes run on your computer, with no account, word cap, or connection required. Wispr Flow transcribes both in its cloud. |

<sub>Competitor details were last verified on September 24, 2026, and October 1, 2026 for Apple Notes, Meetily, and Wispr Flow; each link has the full comparison and sources. Trademarks belong to their owners.</sub>

<a id="privacy--verify-it"></a>

Privacy

Your work is personal. Keeping it local should be the starting point.

Recording and built-in AI processing happen on your computer. LokalBot has no account system, analytics service, or telemetry backend. Your library lives in local files and SQLite under your user account.


flowchart LR

  subgraph mac [Your computer]

    direction LR

    audio["Mic + meeting-app audio"] --> asr["On-device<br/>transcription"]

    asr --> llm["Local summaries<br/>built-in llama.cpp"]

    screen["Opt-in screen text"] --> db[("Local library<br/>full-text + vector search")]

    asr --> db

    llm --> db

    db --> use["Search · Ask · Today · Timeline"]

    db -.->|read-only, off by default| cli["lokalbot-cli · MCP"]

  end
  • You choose what to retain. Activity-only tracking is the default. Visible screen text and encrypted screenshots are opt-in. Pause capture or exclude apps and domains at any time. Detection has limits; exclude anything you never want retained.
  • You control retention. Captured screen text and screenshots expire after 14 days by default. Adjust the window or explicitly save a moment to keep it until you unsave or delete it.
  • Network access has boundaries. Models, updates, and optional agent runtimes need downloads. Automatic update checks can be disabled. A remote model server receives context only after you approve its origin; optional Agent Mode and external CLI/MCP clients have separate permissions and data handling.

To check the local processing path, download the models, select the built-in backend, disable automatic update checks, and observe network traffic while recording, transcribing, and summarizing. Approved agent commands and external clients are separate paths.

[Read the full privacy policy](PRIVACY.md) · [Report a security issue privately](SECURITY.md)

<a id="download"></a>

Get started

LokalBot runs on Apple Silicon Macs with macOS 15 or later. Windows and Linux are in alpha. You'll also need space for your selected models: Settings → Models shows download sizes and readiness, and storage and memory needs depend on the models you choose.

| | macOS | Windows (alpha) | Linux (alpha) |

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Runs on | Apple Silicon (M1 or later), macOS 15+ | Windows 10 or 11, x64 | x86_64 with glibc 2.39 or later (Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Fedora 40 or newer), PulseAudio or PipeWire, and a Vulkan or OpenGL driver |

| Install | LokalBot-<version>-macos-arm64.dmg: drag LokalBot to Applications. Or brew install --cask stevyhacker/tap/lokalbot. | LokalBot-<version>-windows-x86_64-setup.exe: run it to install LokalBot for your user, with a Start menu shortcut and no administrator rights. It isn't code-signed yet, so SmartScreen asks first: More info → Run anyway. The same release has a portable zip. | LokalBot-<version>-linux-x86_64.tar.gz: extract it and run ./install.sh, which adds LokalBot to your applications menu. Or install the .deb (Debian, Ubuntu), .rpm (Fedora, openSUSE) or Arch package from the same release. The .deb, and the .rpm on Fedora, add the LokalBot repository, so sudo apt upgrade or sudo dnf upgrade brings later versions; with the Arch package, LokalBot tells you about updates instead of installing them. |

| Your library | ~/Library/Application Support/me.dotenv.LokalBot | %LOCALAPPDATA%\LokalBot | ~/.local/share/LokalBot |

A library recorded on one platform opens on the others. Not every Mac feature is on Windows and Linux yet; see [what works where](LinuxWindows/README.md#what-works-where).

1. Install the app for your platform and open it.

2. Choose what to capture. Review recording settings: automatic detection, ask-first, or manual recording. Day tracking starts with activity only; saving screen text or screenshots is a separate opt-in. Grant only the permissions for the features you enable.

3. Let the models download. Built-in transcription, search, summaries, and writing can then work offline. No model server to set up and no API key to bring.

Try this first: make a short test recording, let it transcribe, then search for a phrase you said and open the matching passage. Add screen memory or writing tools when you're ready.

Let meeting participants know before recording and get their consent.

Release notes · [Setup help](SUPPORT.md) · [Homebrew options](Distribution/homebrew/README.md) · [Windows and Linux guide](LinuxWindows/README.md)

FAQ

<details>

<summary><strong>Does a bot join my meetings?</strong></summary>

No. LokalBot records your microphone and the meeting app's audio on your computer. On Windows and Linux it records everything the computer plays, not one app. Audio sources are separate from individual speaker identification. When system-audio capture is unavailable, the app warns that recording is microphone-only. Always record with participants' consent.

</details>

<details>

<summary><strong>Does it record everything on my screen?</strong></summary>

No. New installs use activity-only tracking, which you can turn off. Saving visible text or screenshots requires a separate choice and the relevant macOS permissions (on Linux, your desktop's accessibility and screenshot support). Excluded apps and domains and secure fields are skipped; private browser windows are captured unless you exclude the browser or site. Detected credentials are redacted and associated pixels are dropped, but detection is not perfect. See [PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md).

</details>

<details>

<summary><strong>Can I take my notes elsewhere?</strong></summary>

Yes. On Mac, turn on Meeting note export to keep a Markdown note for every meeting in a folder you choose, such as an Obsidian vault or a Logseq graph: the summary, action items, the people and projects involved, and the transcript. You can also export a single meeting, write a daily memory note, or let local routines save drafts. These are ordinary, unencrypted files; any service you sync them with has its own privacy settings. See Meeting transcripts in Obsidian. Note export isn't on Windows and Linux yet.

</details>

<details>

<summary><strong>Does it run on Windows or Linux?</strong></summary>

Yes, as an alpha. The Windows and Linux app is a native Rust app with the same pages, the same models for summaries and search, and the same library format, so a library moves between computers. Selection actions, meeting note export, Personal Context, spoken summaries, and coding-agent sessions in day memory are Mac only for now, and on Wayland some features depend on your desktop. See [what works where](LinuxWindows/README.md#what-works-where).

</details>

Local AI, your choice

Start with the built-in models, then change them in Settings → Models. LokalBot supports its bundled llama.cpp runtime, Ollama, OpenAI-compatible servers, and Apple Intelligence on supported Macs running macOS 26 or later. Think can also run on your own ChatGPT plan (Sign in with ChatGPT) or Claude plan (through your signed-in Claude Code), without an API key, and Agent Mode can run on the ChatGPT plan. Remote servers and plans require approval before receiving context.

Different jobs use different models. These are the Mac defaults on a fresh install, about 9.6 GB of model files if you use every role. They are not a RAM requirement:

| Role | Default model | Format | Approx. model files |

| --- | --- | --- | ---: |

| Transcription | Qwen3-ASR 1.7B | MLX 8-bit | 2.47 GB |

| Summaries and chat | Qwen3.5 4B | Q4_K_M | 2.74 GB |

| Autocomplete | Gemma 4 E2B Base | Q6_K | 3.85 GB |

| Semantic search | EmbeddingGemma 2 | Q8_0 | 0.31 GB |

| Speaker diarization | Nemotron 3 (preview) via FluidAudio | Core ML | ~0.20 GB |

Qwen3-ASR covers 52 languages and dialects. Transcription alternatives include Parakeet, Granite Speech, Whisper large-v3 turbo, SenseVoice for Chinese, Japanese, and Korean, and GigaAM for Russian; Pyannote Community-1 remains available for diarization. The Lightweight preset swaps in smaller models, including LFM2.5 1.2B Instruct (0.73 GB) for autocomplete. Model choices can vary by release; Settings shows the active selections and available presets. Speed and memory use depend on your computer, model, context length, and other workloads.

On Windows and Linux, transcription uses Qwen3-ASR 0.6B through sherpa-onnx (Parakeet v3, SenseVoice, and Whisper turbo are optional), speakers are separated with pyannote segmentation and TitaNet, and autocomplete uses LFM2.5 1.2B by default. Summaries (Qwen3.5 4B) and search (EmbeddingGemma 2) use the same models as on Mac. The default download is about 4 GB, and llama.cpp runs on a Vulkan GPU or the CPU.

[Project benchmarks](Benchmarks/README.md) · [Model catalog](LokalBot/Engines/ModelCatalog.swift) · [Search implementation](LokalBot/Services/EmbeddingIndex.swift) · [Model and runtime details](DEVELOPMENT.md#built-in-llm-runtime--llamacpp--model-catalog)

For developers & agents

The app bundles lokalbot-cli, a read-only interface to your meeting library and a stdio Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. Access is off by default. Enable meeting-library access in Settings → Privacy & Data, then install the CLI from Settings → Advanced → Agent CLI.

<div align="center"><img src="Assets/cli-demo.svg" alt="Animated terminal session: lokalbot-cli lists meetings as a table, searches transcripts for redis and returns JSON, then prints the latest meeting summary" width="720" /></div>


lokalbot-cli search "database decision"

lokalbot-cli get latest --include metadata,summary

lokalbot-cli mcp

Without a PATH installation, use /Applications/LokalBot.app/Contents/Helpers/lokalbot-cli on Mac. On Windows and Linux, Settings → Advanced → Agent CLI installs it too; see [Coding agents](LinuxWindows/README.md#coding-agents) for where it goes and how to add it to your PATH. There the CLI has the read-only commands and every MCP tool; ask, reply, and the setup and configuration commands are Mac only.

Connect Claude Code with one command, or install the [Claude Code plugin](Distribution/claude-plugin/README.md):


# macOS

claude mcp add lokalbot -- /Applications/LokalBot.app/Contents/Helpers/lokalbot-cli mcp

# Windows and Linux, with lokalbot-cli on your PATH

claude mcp add lokalbot -- lokalbot-cli mcp

Screen-memory MCP tools require separate permission scoped to today, the last seven days, or all retained history. They return text and metadata, not decrypted screenshots. External clients may send results to their own model providers.

The app also has an optional Agent Mode for working with reviewed context. File and shell actions follow its approval settings; it is separate from the read-only CLI/MCP interface.

[CLI examples](.agents/skills/lokalbot-cli/SKILL.md) · [Claude Code plugin](Distribution/claude-plugin/README.md) · [MCP architecture](DEVELOPMENT.md#agent-cli--mcp)

Build from source

For the Mac app, use an Apple Silicon Mac with full Xcode installed; the [build workflow](.github/workflows/build.yml) pins the CI toolchain. With Homebrew available:


brew install xcodegen cmake



git clone https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot.git

cd lokalbot



# XcodeGen needs these paths before the first build fetches the runtimes.

mkdir -p Vendor/llama-cpp Vendor/sherpa-onnx

xcodegen generate

open LokalBot.xcodeproj

Select LokalBot Dev, set your signing team, and run. The Dev app has its own identity, macOS permission grants, library, model storage, and Keychain namespace, so it can live alongside the installed release without applying development retention settings to release data. The first build prepares pinned native runtimes; model downloads happen separately.

For the Windows and Linux app, see [Build from source](LinuxWindows/README.md#build-from-source) in its README (Rust).

[Build and test commands](DEVELOPMENT.md#build-workflows) · [Testing guide](DEVELOPMENT.md#testing) · [Screenshot guide](Docs/screenshot-kit.md)

<details>

<summary><strong>Find your way around the code</strong></summary>


LokalBot/

├── Views/       # Native SwiftUI screens, settings, and onboarding

├── Services/    # Recording, search, storage, and workday memory

├── Engines/     # Transcription, model catalog, and local inference

├── Cotyping/    # System-wide autocomplete

├── Dictation/   # Voice typing

└── Agent/       # Optional Agent Mode and approval flow

CLI/             # Command-line interface and MCP entry points

LinuxWindows/    # Windows and Linux app (Rust + GPUI)

LokalBotTests/   # Unit tests

Scripts/         # Build, verification, capture, and release tooling

project.yml      # XcodeGen source of truth

</details>

<a id="contributing--security"></a>

Contributing

Bug reports, documentation improvements, and code contributions are welcome. Report an issue with steps to reproduce, expected and actual behavior, the app version, your OS and its version (on Linux, also the distribution, desktop, and X11 or Wayland), your chip or CPU and GPU, RAM, and selected models. Keep private recordings and transcripts out of reports.

For larger changes, open an issue to discuss the approach first. Follow the [working agreements](AGENTS.md) and [development guide](DEVELOPMENT.md), keep pull requests focused, and record your checks in the [PR template](.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md). Include screenshots for UI changes; run UI tests on hosted CI or a remote runner.

License & acknowledgements

LokalBot is free software under [GPLv3](LICENSE). Code in the Autocomplete engine that was ported from Cotabby stays under [AGPLv3](LICENSES/AGPL-3.0.txt). Other third-party components and models retain their own licenses; see [third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

Built with llama.cpp, MLX Swift, speech-swift, sherpa-onnx, WhisperKit, FluidAudio, Sparkle, XcodeGen, GPUI, GPUI Kit, and ONNX Runtime, with models including Qwen3-ASR, IBM Granite Speech, Parakeet, and LFM2.5. The Autocomplete engine started from Cotabby's open-source code.
skillMd:
---
name: lokalbot-cli
description: The user's local memory of their meetings, screen, coding-agent work, and what they shared about themselves. Run `lokalbot-cli brief` at the start of a session on the user's own work, and check LokalBot before asking the user about past work, decisions, commitments, or where something stands. Also use it to look up how LokalBot is configured.
---

# LokalBot CLI Skill

LokalBot is a private work-memory app for macOS, Linux and Windows. Its read-only CLI retrieves recorded meetings; separately authorized MCP tools retrieve screen-memory text and metadata. Use this skill for evidence from the user's recorded work, not for scheduling meetings or answering general questions about a topic.

If `lokalbot-cli` isn't on PATH, use the embedded copy directly:
`/Applications/LokalBot.app/Contents/Helpers/lokalbot-cli`.
Windows and Linux installs put it at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\LokalBot\bin\lokalbot-cli.exe` (Windows) or `~/.local/bin/lokalbot-cli` (Linux).

## Start here

```bash
lokalbot-cli brief
```

Run this once at the start of a session (MCP: `get_briefing`). It says which LokalBot sources are on and how the user would turn on the others, then gives what each permission covers: what the user shared about themselves, their open action items, current projects and goals, recent Claude Code and Codex work by project, and a timeline with recent days in detail and older weeks and months in a line each. It is short on purpose. Use it to orient, then search for detail. `brief` points to `lokalbot-cli` commands; `get_briefing` gives the same text but names MCP tools instead.

Before asking the user about past work, a decision, a commitment, or where something stands, search LokalBot first. Ask only when LokalBot has nothing, and say what you checked. Items the briefing doesn't list are unknown, not false. Cite meetings from `get`, `search`, or `actions` results, not from the briefing's summary lines.

## Choose the source

- Use `list` when you need candidate meeting ids, titles, and dates.
- Use `list --include summary` for what several meetings covered, such as the topics of the last ten meetings or one week's themes. One call returns every summary, shortened to fit. Don't fetch transcripts meeting by meeting for that: they are long, and ten of them can fill your context.
- Use `get` when the meeting is known; `latest` works without listing first. Request `metadata,summary` for a cited summary; include `transcript` when the question needs exact wording.
- Use `search` directly when the user remembers a phrase or wants cross-meeting mentions.
- Use `actions` for commitments: what the user owes, overdue work, or one meeting's next steps.
- Use `people` for everything about one person: what the user owes them, what they owe the user, decisions made together, and shared meetings.
- Use `path` only when the task needs an on-disk folder or audio file.
- For viewed screen text or app activity, use the screen-memory MCP tools within the user's separate permission and history scope.
- Use `personal-context` (MCP: `get_personal_context`) before advising on a personal decision or tailoring work to the user: it returns the facts, preferences, goals, and principles the user chose to share, most relevant to your task first.

## Discovery

```bash
lokalbot-cli list --limit 10
lokalbot-cli list --limit 10 --table
lokalbot-cli list --since 2026-06-01 --query "design"
lokalbot-cli list --limit 10 --include summary
lokalbot-cli list --since 2026-10-13 --until 2026-10-17 --include summary --table
```

The `id` field in each list entry is an 8-character prefix that the other commands accept.

`--include summary` adds each meeting's `summary` (Markdown). The listed summaries share 20,000 characters: short ones come whole, and a long one is cut, ending in `…`, with `"summary_truncated": true`. `get <id> --include summary` reads it whole. With `--include summary`, `--limit` defaults to 10 and goes up to 50. `transcript` isn't accepted there; read transcripts one meeting at a time with `get`.

## Reading a single meeting

```bash
lokalbot-cli get latest --include metadata,summary
lokalbot-cli get 4f7c2a91 --include metadata,summary --format json
lokalbot-cli get 4f7c2a91 --include metadata,transcript
```

`--include` accepts a comma-separated list of `metadata`, `summary`, `transcript`. Default is all three.

## Cross-meeting search

```bash
lokalbot-cli search "auth refactor"
lokalbot-cli search "auth refactor" --table --limit 20
```

A meeting matches when it contains every word, in any order, ignoring case and accents; when none does, the closest partial matches follow. Words of up to three letters or digits (`API`, `Q3`) match only whole words. Quote an exact phrase inside the query (`'"auth refactor"'`) to match only that phrase. Transcript hits include a `timestamp` (HH:MM:SS) so the user can jump to that moment in the in-app player.

## Answers and reply drafts

These two commands are in the Mac app's CLI only. On Windows and Linux, use the `ask_library` MCP tool for answers, and draft replies yourself from `search` and `get` results.

```bash
lokalbot-cli ask "What did we decide about the caching layer?"
lokalbot-cli reply "Did you pick a caching layer yet?" --instruction "keep it short"
pbpaste | lokalbot-cli reply
```

`ask` is the command-line form of `ask_library` (below): LokalBot's local model answers from the matching meetings. `reply` drafts the user's reply to a message they received from what the matching meetings say, without inventing facts; a message no meeting matches gets no draft. Both need the LokalBot app running, and the first call after a cold start can take up to a minute. JSON by default: `{"status", "text", "sources"}`, where `status` is `answered`, `not_found`, or `error` (with a `code` such as `access_disabled`); errors also exit with status 1. Show a draft to the user before sending it anywhere.

## Action items

```bash
lokalbot-cli actions
lokalbot-cli actions --owner me --table
lokalbot-cli actions --owner ana --status all --days 90
lokalbot-cli actions --meeting 4f7c2a91
```

Actions use the user's saved corrections and status. `due_date` (YYYY-MM-DD) appears only when the spoken due phrase resolves unambiguously; otherwise use `due` as said. Overdue and soon-due work comes first.

## People

```bash
lokalbot-cli people --table
lokalbot-cli people --query ana
lokalbot-cli people "Ana Petrović"
```

People are joined from calendar attendee names, speaker names applied in LokalBot, and action owners. Names chosen, people merged, and entries hidden on the app's People page apply here too, and `meeting_count` counts a call recorded in several parts once. Only names are returned; never ask for or infer email addresses.

## Personal context

```bash
lokalbot-cli personal-context --task "Evaluate a job offer in Berlin"
lokalbot-cli personal-context --task "Plan next quarter" --kind goal --kind principle --limit 5
```

Items are the user's own statements (`authority: "stated"`), shared by them for agents. Use them only when they bear on the task, and say which ones shaped your answer. Items not returned are unknown, not false, so don't infer the user's values from their absence. They are not evidence about meetings or other people. A `[personal_context_disabled]` error means the user hasn't turned on "Allow external agents to read what I shared about myself" in Settings → Privacy. Explain that, and don't work around it. The Windows and Linux app has no such setting or About you page yet, so there personal context is on only in a library that came from a Mac.

## Path lookup

```bash
lokalbot-cli path
lokalbot-cli path latest
cd "$(lokalbot-cli path latest)"
```

## Settings and status

Use these when the user asks how LokalBot is set up, why something is or isn't happening (recording, capture, models), or wants a setting changed. They are in the Mac app's CLI only. On Windows and Linux, tell the user where the setting is in LokalBot's Settings and let them change it there.

```bash
lokalbot-cli config search "dark mode"           # find a setting's key by plain words
lokalbot-cli config describe autoRecordMode      # type, allowed values, tier
lokalbot-cli config get autoRecordMode
lokalbot-cli config list --changed --table
lokalbot-cli config set noteTemplate=lecture summaryLanguage=en
lokalbot-cli config set trackingEnabled=false --dry-run
lokalbot-cli config reset dayDigestHour
lokalbot-cli config export --changed > settings.json
lokalbot-cli config import settings.json --dry-run
lokalbot-cli config set calendarDetectionEnabled=true --wait 120   # waits for the user's approval
lokalbot-cli config request <id> --wait 120      # answer to an earlier needs_approval
lokalbot-cli secret list                         # which API keys are saved (never their values)
printf %s "$KEY" | lokalbot-cli secret set openai-compatible --wait 120
lokalbot-cli status                              # version, recording, models, permissions, agent access
lokalbot-cli open settings dictationShortcut     # show the user a setting in LokalBot
lokalbot-cli open settings permissions           # or a section
```

`search`, `describe`, and `config schema` work any time. Everything else needs the separate "Allow external agents to change LokalBot settings" toggle in LokalBot → Settings → Privacy. If a command returns `[settings_access_disabled]`, explain that setting and let the user choose. These commands start LokalBot in the background when it isn't running; pass `--no-launch` when the user doesn't want it started.

Changing settings:

- Change only what the user asked for. Run `describe` first so you use the right tokens, and `--dry-run` when you are unsure. A `set` applies all of its pairs or none of them.
- Preferences (tier `preference`), and changes that narrow what LokalBot captures or sends (turning capture off, adding an exclusion), apply right away. The user can undo them under the toggle.
- Turning on capture, a data source, autocomplete or dictation, approving a server, removing an exclusion, or changing retention (tier `consent`) sends the whole request to the user in LokalBot and returns `[needs_approval]` (exit 3) with the request in `details`: its `id`, every change, and, for a shorter retention policy, what the cleanup deletes. Nothing is applied yet. Ask the user before making such a request, tell them a card is waiting in LokalBot, and pass `--wait <seconds>` (up to 300) or run `config request <id> --wait <seconds>` for the answer: exit 0 approved, 4 declined, 5 expired. Don't resend a declined request unless the user asks; an identical request still waiting is reused rather than asked twice.
- API keys: `secret set <name>` reads the key from standard input and always waits for approval the same way. Never put a key on the command line, never echo it back, and never ask to read one; `secret list` only says whether each is saved. `secret clear <name>` removes one right away.
- `[read_only]` settings can't be changed from the terminal.
- Never write LokalBot's preferences with `defaults write`, and never create or edit files in its `control/` folder: a partial preferences write silently resets other settings (it can turn automatic recording on), and the running app overwrites it anyway.

## Setting up LokalBot

When the user wants LokalBot installed or set up on a Mac, follow [AGENT_SETUP.md](https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot/blob/master/AGENT_SETUP.md). On Windows and Linux there is no agent-driven setup yet; follow that guide's Windows and Linux section, where the user does the setup in the app.

```bash
lokalbot-cli setup start --wait 300        # the user clicks Allow in LokalBot; the only way to get access
lokalbot-cli setup plan > plan.json        # talk it through, then edit to the user's answers
lokalbot-cli setup apply plan.json --wait 300
lokalbot-cli models status                 # poll until meetingReady
lokalbot-cli permissions                   # then: permissions request <name>, restart if macOS asks
lokalbot-cli setup finish
lokalbot-cli doctor                        # exit 0 when ready; nextSteps otherwise
```

- Ask before adding `--meeting-library` or `--screen-memory` to `setup start`, and before requesting any setting in the plan's `notes.needsApproval`.
- Exit 3 means the user hasn't answered yet, 4 means they declined (don't ask again unless they say so), and 5 means the request expired.
- For permissions, tell the user exactly what to click, then poll `permissions` until it shows the grant.
- Never install by removing the quarantine attribute, and never write LokalBot's preferences or files in `control/` yourself.

## MCP alternative (and ask_library)

The same library is available over MCP for GUI clients and anything else that speaks it: `lokalbot-cli mcp` serves `get_briefing` (call it first; same text as `brief`), `list_meetings` (`include: "summary"` works as in `list --include summary`), `get_meeting`, `search_meetings`, `ask_library`, `get_action_items`, `list_people`, and `get_person` on stdio. It also advertises `search_screen`, `get_timeline`, `get_recent_activity`, `get_app_usage`, and `get_screenshot_detail`; those return OCR and metadata only, never decrypted pixels or screenshot paths. `get_personal_context` returns what the user shared about themselves under its own permission.

```bash
claude mcp add lokalbot -- /Applications/LokalBot.app/Contents/Helpers/lokalbot-cli mcp
```

When `lokalbot-cli` is on PATH, `claude mcp add lokalbot -- lokalbot-cli mcp` works on every platform.

`ask_library` is the synthesis tool: it sends the question to LokalBot's **local** model, which reads the library and returns only an answer with meeting citations — useful when the user wants a conclusion rather than quotes. It needs the LokalBot app running, and the first call can take up to a minute while the model loads. Prefer `search`/`get` when the user wants exact wording.

Meeting tools require the user's consent toggle: LokalBot → Settings → Privacy → "Allow external agents to read your meeting library". If a tool returns `[access_disabled]`, explain the setting and let the user choose whether to enable it. Do not change consent markers or work around disabled access.

LokalBot itself does not upload library content. An external agent or MCP client may transmit tool inputs and results under its own privacy terms, so connect only clients the user trusts and retrieve the minimum meeting content needed.

Screen-memory tools require the separate "Allow external agents to read screen memory" toggle. A meeting-library grant never implies a screen-memory grant. If a screen tool returns `[screen_access_disabled]`, explain that separate choice and do not work around it.

## Evidence and privacy

- Answer from returned evidence. Quote exact wording only from retrieved text; distinguish your synthesis from the recorded content. If there are no hits, say so.
- Cite meetings by title and date, adding transcript timestamps for exact moments. Identify the captured time and app for screen-memory evidence when provided.
- Never write into the meetings folder. Audio, transcripts, and summaries live in the `meetings` folder of the library root that `lokalbot-cli path` prints (on a Mac, `~/Library/Application Support/me.dotenv.LokalBot/`).
- Retrieve only the content needed. Summarize instead of pasting full transcripts unless explicitly asked.
- Do not forward transcripts, summaries, or tool results to any additional service beyond the client the user deliberately connected.
